meta.name: SyteNav (work-os-navigator)
meta.description: Construction management platform: quotes, bidding, budgets, schedule, field ops, compliance and money for general contractors and subcontractors. Next.js 14 App Router + Supabase (Postgres/Auth/Storage) on Vercel, with an Anthropic-powered document-reading layer.
meta.purpose: Machine-readable architecture graph for AI agents. Nodes are components, edges are the calls between them, flows are ordered end-to-end paths through those edges.

stack.framework: Next.js 14.2.16 (App Router, React 18, RSC + client components)
stack.styling: Tailwind CSS 3 with CSS-variable design tokens (SyteNav "Field" theme, light + dark)
stack.data: Supabase Postgres, Supabase Auth (cookie sessions via @supabase/ssr), Supabase Storage
stack.ai: @anthropic-ai/sdk, model claude-opus-4-8, vision + PDF document blocks
stack.hosting: Vercel (SSR + serverless route handlers, one daily cron)
stack.mobile: Capacitor remote-URL native shell (loads the deployed web app); dedicated /field mobile shell in-app

layout.rule: Nodes are placed in vertical columns by `layer`, ordered top-to-bottom by `order`. Renderers may compute x = layerIndex * columnWidth and y from `order`, centering each column.

node_kinds.actor: A human or machine that originates traffic
node_kinds.shell: A Next.js route group / layout that frames a set of pages
node_kinds.page: A user-facing screen or cluster of screens
node_kinds.external: Third-party service reached over the network

edge_kinds.fetch: In-app fetch to an internal API route
edge_kinds.external: Outbound call to a third-party API
edge_kinds.event: Side effect written for someone else to read (notification, activity log)

conventions.auth: Browser sessions are Supabase cookies, refreshed in middleware.ts. Route handlers authenticate with an `Authorization: Bearer <supabase access token>` header, resolved by `db.auth.getUser(token)`.
conventions.db_access: 149 of 157 route handlers instantiate a Supabase client with SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY, which bypasses RLS. Row-level security is enabled on the base tables (18 ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY statements in 001_initial_schema.sql) but the service-role path means authorization is enforced in route code, not by the database.
conventions.authorization: The permission model lives in lib/permissions.ts (32 resources x view/create/edit/delete). The client resolves it via /api/me/permissions and hides UI; server-side re-checks exist in lib/server-permissions.ts (`getActor`/`actorCan`) but are currently wired into app/api/projects/route.ts plus the settings permission endpoints. Most other handlers authenticate the user and scope queries by company/project rather than consulting the permission grid.
conventions.no_account_access: Subs, clients, architects and inspectors act through unguessable tokens in the URL (bid_invites.token, rfis.answer_token, compliance_requests.token, projects.client_portal_token, profiles.calendar_token). Those routes intentionally skip auth.
conventions.activity: Cross-cutting writes go through lib/log-activity.ts (project_activity) and lib/notify.ts (notifications); the Recent Activity feed and the bell both read those tables.
conventions.ai_review: Every AI extraction returns a draft the user reviews and edits before anything is saved.

nodes.label: Office user
nodes.summary: Owner, admin, project manager or office staff working in the full desktop/responsive app.
nodes.detail: Sees the (dashboard) shell: sidebar, top nav, project tabs. Role decides which tabs and actions exist.

nodes.label: Field crew
nodes.summary: Worker or field member on a phone. Routed to the stripped-down Field Mode shell.
nodes.detail: FIELD_ROLES = ['worker','member'] in lib/permissions.ts. Field supervisors stay in the full app because they need budget/compliance breadth.

nodes.label: Subcontractor
nodes.summary: Sub company with an account: receives bid invites, submits quotes, runs awarded jobs.
nodes.detail: Company type drives sub-specific views (My Bids, My Jobs, quote-line-items-as-budget).

nodes.label: Client / architect (no account)
nodes.summary: Clients, architects, inspectors and un-registered subs who act purely through secure token links.
nodes.detail: Client portal, RFI answer link, compliance upload link, bid submission link, sign-off link. No login, no Supabase user.

nodes.label: Platform super admin
nodes.summary: Emails listed in lib/super-admin.ts. Can open /admin and impersonate any account for support.
nodes.detail: Gated twice: super-admin email allowlist, then an HMAC-signed PIN cookie (lib/admin-gate.ts).

nodes.label: Capacitor native shell
nodes.summary: iOS/Android wrapper that loads the deployed web app over https rather than bundling a static export.
nodes.detail: A static export is not viable (SSR + 157 route handlers + middleware), so capacitor.config.ts points server.url at the production domain and allowlists only that origin plus *.supabase.co.

nodes.label: Calendar app
nodes.summary: Google / Apple / Outlook subscribing to the read-only iCal feed.
nodes.detail: Calendar clients cannot send auth headers, so the feed is protected only by profiles.calendar_token in the URL.

nodes.label: Vercel Cron
nodes.summary: Daily 08:07 UTC trigger declared in vercel.json.
nodes.detail: Hits /api/cron/compliance-reminders. Authenticated by the x-vercel-cron header, or CRON_SECRET when called manually.

nodes.label: middleware.ts
nodes.summary: Runs on every non-asset request: refreshes the Supabase cookie session and redirects based on auth state.
nodes.detail: Protects /dashboard, /projects, /directory, /approvals, /settings. Logged-out root goes to /homepage; logged-in visitors on /login, /signup or / go to /dashboard. Cookie writes are mirrored onto the response so the session stays fresh.

nodes.label: /homepage (marketing)
nodes.summary: Public marketing site: features, workflow walkthrough, AI, pricing, security, GC and sub audience pages, legal.
nodes.detail: 16 pages plus a bespoke component kit (scroll hero, phone fan, device mocks, stat marquee). Also drives robots.ts, sitemap.ts and OG/Twitter image routes.

nodes.label: (auth) shell
nodes.summary: Login, signup, forgot-password, reset-password and the OAuth/magic-link callback.

nodes.label: (dashboard) shell
nodes.summary: The office app frame: sidebar, top nav, impersonation and view-as banners, idle logout, delete-guard provider.
nodes.detail: Server component. Redirects unauthenticated users to /login and FIELD_ROLES users to /field. All chrome is print:hidden so invoice / pay-app / proposal print views render clean.

nodes.label: /field (Field Mode)
nodes.summary: Dedicated mobile shell for field workers: no sidebar, no project tabs, no company money.
nodes.detail: Bottom nav only. Office roles that land here bounce to /dashboard; admins and managers may enter to preview it.

nodes.label: /admin console
nodes.summary: Platform-owner console behind a PIN gate: companies, users, projects, access requests, audit log.

nodes.label: Token pages (no auth)
nodes.summary: Standalone pages reached by secret link: /bid/[token], /rfi/[token], /compliance/[token], /portal/[token].
nodes.detail: Rendered outside every authenticated layout. Each one talks to its matching public API route.

nodes.label: Dashboard & cross-project
nodes.summary: Home dashboard, Master Calendar and Master Money.
nodes.detail: Stat cards, cash-in vs cash-out chart, this-week agenda, recent projects and the Recent Activity drawer. Master views roll every job into one calendar and one money sheet.

nodes.label: Projects list / map / new
nodes.summary: Grid, list and Leaflet map of every job, plus the create-project form.
nodes.detail: Search by name/address/client, filter by status and type, edit inline (including sq ft and billing mode), delete with confirmation. Address autocomplete + geocoding drops map pins.

nodes.label: Project · Field tabs
nodes.summary: Plans, Schedule, Tasks, Progress, Daily Logs, Time Clock.
nodes.detail: Plan viewer with zoom and pins, schedule with crew-overlap warnings, tasks with sign-off, daily logs with photos and PDF export, weekly timesheets with approval.

nodes.label: Project · People tabs
nodes.summary: Team, Bids, RFIs.
nodes.detail: Team assignment drives assigned-only scoping for field roles. Bids covers packages, invitations, reminders and awards. RFIs can carry change-order proposals.

nodes.label: Project · Money tabs
nodes.summary: Budget, Invoices, Pay Apps, Payments, Request Quotes, Compare Quotes, Financials, Change Orders.
nodes.detail: Which tabs appear depends on the project's billing_mode: Simple invoicing shows Invoices + Payments, AIA progress billing shows Pay Apps with retainage.

nodes.label: Project · Compliance tabs
nodes.summary: Permits, Inspections, Submittals, Compliance, Reports.

nodes.label: Workspace tools
nodes.summary: Directory, Customers, Files, Equipment, Materials, Approvals.
nodes.detail: Company-wide, not project-scoped. Approvals is the single inbox for anything awaiting a decision; Materials is the receipt-scanning surface.

nodes.label: My Bids / My Jobs
nodes.summary: The subcontractor side of the app: incoming invites and awarded work across every GC.
nodes.detail: Subs submit and revise quotes with line items and payment terms, then track scope, schedule and payment stages, and mark work Ready for Inspection.

nodes.label: Settings & permissions
nodes.summary: Company profile and logo, team invites, the permission grid, custom role classes, delete-protection key, budget templates, QuickBooks card, calendar connect.

nodes.label: Help Center
nodes.summary: 40+ support articles with client-side keyword search, kept in sync with every feature change.
nodes.detail: Article content is a typed data structure in lib/help/articles.ts, not a CMS.

nodes.label: Print / PDF views
nodes.summary: Printable invoice, pay application (G702/G703) and proposal pages.
nodes.detail: Rendered inside the dashboard shell with all chrome hidden by print: variants, so browser print or save-as-PDF gives a clean document.

nodes.label: Field Mode pages
nodes.summary: Today, Tasks, Log and Me: the four screens a field worker gets.
nodes.detail: Clock card with selfie capture and GPS, task rows with one-tap status, quick daily-log filing.

nodes.label: Admin console pages
nodes.summary: Platform stats, companies, users, projects, access requests, impersonation audit.

nodes.label: usePermissions + View As
nodes.summary: Client hook that loads the caller's effective permission map and exposes can(resource, action).
nodes.detail: Reads localStorage keys workos_view_as_role / workos_view_as_user so admins can preview the app as another role or a specific teammate; the preview is resolved server-side by /api/me/permissions.

nodes.label: useViewerContext
nodes.summary: Tells a project screen whether the viewer's company owns the job and what company type they are.
nodes.detail: Switches sub-specific rendering, e.g. a sub's standalone job where quote line items are the budget.

nodes.label: Supabase browser client
nodes.summary: createBrowserClient from @supabase/ssr. Owns the session and mints the bearer token every fetch attaches.

nodes.label: /api/me/*
nodes.summary: permissions and tasks for the signed-in user.
nodes.detail: /api/me/permissions is the authoritative permission resolver: role defaults -> company_roles overrides (including custom classes) -> per-user permission_overrides, with admin-only as_user / as preview parameters.

nodes.label: /api/dashboard/*, /api/master/*
nodes.summary: Cross-project rollups: overview, stats, activity feed, master calendar, master money.

nodes.label: /api/projects (core)
nodes.summary: Project CRUD, bulk actions, stats, geocoding, per-project activity, viewer context, portal token minting.
nodes.detail: app/api/projects/route.ts is the one handler that fully applies the server-side permission grid via getActor/actorCan.

nodes.label: /api/projects/[id] field routes
nodes.summary: Plans and folders, plan pins, schedule, job schedule, tasks and notes, daily logs with photos and PDF, time clock.
nodes.detail: Includes the geofenced punch endpoint and the payroll hours export.

nodes.label: Bidding & quotes API
nodes.summary: Bid requests and invites, bid packages, remind/revise, award, quote comparisons and awards, subcontracts.

nodes.label: Money API
nodes.summary: Budget lines and sign-offs, budget templates, invoices with documents and lien waivers, pay applications, client payments, change orders, financials, materials.
nodes.detail: Pay-app creation carries previous_completed forward from prior applications and defaults retainage from the project or company setting.

nodes.label: Compliance API
nodes.summary: Permits, inspections and inspection cards, submittals, compliance documents and email requests.

nodes.label: Workspace API
nodes.summary: Customers, directory companies and profiles, files and file packets, equipment and assignments, notifications, approvals inbox.

nodes.label: /api/search
nodes.summary: Global search across projects, customers, companies, files and more, returned as grouped hits with hrefs.
nodes.detail: Escapes PostgREST or() reserved characters so a query containing a comma or percent sign cannot break the filter string.

nodes.label: /api/my-bids, /api/my-jobs
nodes.summary: The subcontractor's cross-GC view of invites and awarded jobs.

nodes.label: Settings & onboarding API
nodes.summary: Company settings, logo, teammates, member roles and per-user permission overrides, custom role classes, calendar token, delete-key verification, invites, signup completion, access requests.
nodes.detail: The settings permission endpoints are among the few that re-check authorization on the server.

nodes.label: /api/admin/*
nodes.summary: Platform stats, companies, users, projects, access requests, audit, PIN verification and impersonation.
nodes.detail: Impersonation mints a one-time magic-link token_hash for the target user so the browser gets a real session. Also hosts /api/dev/seed-demo behind DEMO_SEED_SECRET.

nodes.label: AI extraction endpoints
nodes.summary: The 11 handlers that send a document or photo to Claude and return a reviewable draft.
nodes.detail: Quote scan, bid-request to comparison, quote gap analysis, subcontractor proposal analysis, material receipt scan, permit scan, compliance document scan, inspection card, submittal analysis. All use model claude-opus-4-8 with base64 image or PDF document blocks, strip code fences, and fall back to null on any parse failure rather than throwing.

nodes.label: Public token API
nodes.summary: Unauthenticated endpoints backing the token pages: bid submission, RFI answer, compliance upload.
nodes.detail: Each looks the token up, marks it viewed on first open, and accepts a submission. No session is ever created.

nodes.label: /api/calendar/[token]
nodes.summary: Read-only iCal feed keyed by profiles.calendar_token.
nodes.detail: Emits escaped VEVENTs for project dates so Google/Apple/Outlook can subscribe.

nodes.label: /api/cron/compliance-reminders
nodes.summary: Daily sweep for compliance documents expiring within 30 days.
nodes.detail: Notifies every profile at the owning company, then stamps reminder_sent_at and flips status to expiring_soon so a document only fires once per expiry cycle.

nodes.label: Integration proxies
nodes.summary: QuickBooks OAuth and sync, address autocomplete and details, weather.
nodes.detail: Every third-party key stays server-side; the browser only ever talks to these proxies.

nodes.label: lib/permissions.ts
nodes.summary: The permission model: 32 resources in 6 groups x view/create/edit/delete, plus role defaults for admin, manager, project_manager, office_staff, field_supervisor, worker, member and read_only.
nodes.detail: Also defines ASSIGNED_ONLY_ROLES (field roles see only projects they are on) and FIELD_ROLES (who gets Field Mode). resolveRoleBase layers a company's company_roles row over the hardcoded defaults, or starts from all-none for a brand-new custom class.

nodes.label: lib/server-permissions.ts
nodes.summary: getActor(db, token) resolves a bearer token into { userId, role, companyId, permissions }; actorCan gates an action.
nodes.detail: Mirrors /api/me/permissions exactly so what the UI hides is what the API refuses. Currently wired into app/api/projects/route.ts.

nodes.label: lib/log-activity.ts
nodes.summary: Single writer for the project_activity event log.
nodes.detail: Called from ~40 handlers covering RFIs, change orders, invoices, tasks, awards, permits, inspections, submittals, daily logs, subcontracts, bid packages, receipts, payments, equipment, punches, team changes and budget edits.

nodes.label: lib/notify.ts
nodes.summary: Inserts an in-app notification row for a user.
nodes.detail: Feeds the notification bell. Types include task_assigned, bid_awarded, invoice_approved, compliance_expiring.

nodes.label: lib/admin-gate.ts
nodes.summary: HMAC-signs the /admin PIN cookie against the user id so it cannot be forged or reused by another account.
nodes.detail: Verified with timingSafeEqual. Secret is SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY.

nodes.label: lib/super-admin.ts
nodes.summary: Hardcoded allowlist of platform-owner emails permitted to impersonate any account.

nodes.label: lib/delete-key.ts
nodes.summary: SHA-256 of the company's secret delete key, checked before destructive actions when delete protection is on.

nodes.label: lib/compliance-extract.ts
nodes.summary: Normalises AI output for insurance certificates and licences into typed fields plus a human summary.

nodes.label: lib/quickbooks.ts
nodes.summary: QuickBooks Online OAuth2 and API helper: authorize URL, token exchange and refresh, sandbox/production base URLs, minor version 73.
nodes.detail: Phase 1 is a one-way push from SyteNav to QBO. Requires QBO_CLIENT_ID and QBO_CLIENT_SECRET; qboConfigured() lets the UI degrade gracefully when they are absent.

nodes.label: Service-role client
nodes.summary: createClient(URL, SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY) instantiated per handler in 149 of 157 routes.
nodes.detail: Bypasses row-level security, so any tenant scoping must be written into the query. The cookie-based server client (lib/supabase/server.ts) is used by the four server components that need the session.

nodes.label: Supabase Auth
nodes.summary: Email/password sessions, password reset, magic links (also used to mint impersonation sessions).
nodes.detail: Cookie session refreshed by middleware; route handlers verify the bearer access token.

nodes.label: Identity & company tables
nodes.summary: profiles, companies, company_roles, company_invites, access_requests, impersonation_log, contacts, customers.
nodes.detail: profiles carries role, company_id, permission_overrides (jsonb), phone and calendar_token. company_roles stores per-company overrides of role defaults and custom classes.

nodes.label: Project tables
nodes.summary: projects, project_team_members, project_activity.
nodes.detail: projects holds status, type, address, latitude/longitude, interior/exterior sq ft, billing_mode, default_retainage_pct, quote file and totals, payment_stages and client_portal_token.

nodes.label: Field tables
nodes.summary: project_plans, plan_folders, plan_pins, tasks, project_tasks, task_notes, schedule_items, daily_logs, daily_log_photos, daily_log_updates, daily_log_attachments, time_entries, equipment, equipment_assignments.

nodes.label: Bidding tables
nodes.summary: bid_packages, bids, bid_invitations, bid_package_attachments, bid_requests, bid_invites, bid_submissions, bid_request_attachments, quotes, quote_comparisons, subcontracts.
nodes.detail: Two generations coexist: the original bid_packages/bids/bid_invitations set and the newer bid_requests/bid_invites/bid_submissions set added in migration 024.

nodes.label: Money tables
nodes.summary: budget_line_items, budget_templates, budget_template_items, invoices, pay_applications, pay_application_lines, client_payments, change_orders, payment_schedule_items, material_purchases.
nodes.detail: budget_line_items links to subcontracts so Committed auto-fills and Actual accrues from approved invoices plus assigned receipts. pay_application_lines carry scheduled_value, previous_completed, this_period and materials_stored for G703.

nodes.label: Compliance tables
nodes.summary: permits, inspections, submittals, compliance_documents, compliance_requests, rfis.
nodes.detail: compliance_documents track expiry_date, status and reminder_sent_at for the nightly sweep. rfis carry answer_token for the public answer link.

nodes.label: Ops & integration tables
nodes.summary: notifications, company_files, file_packets, quickbooks_connections, quickbooks_oauth_states, quickbooks_sync_log.

nodes.label: Supabase Storage
nodes.summary: Buckets for plans, photos, receipts, submittals, signatures, logos and generated documents.
nodes.detail: Named buckets in code include daily-log-photos (also used for clock-in selfies), submittals, company-files, plans, signatures, lien-waivers, proposals and rfi-attachments. Files are handed out as long-lived signed URLs.

nodes.label: Anthropic Claude API
nodes.summary: Reads quotes, receipts, invoices, permits, insurance certificates and submittals from PDFs and phone photos.
nodes.detail: model claude-opus-4-8, max_tokens up to 8192, base64 document/image content blocks. Requires ANTHROPIC_API_KEY.

nodes.label: QuickBooks Online
nodes.summary: Intuit OAuth2 plus the accounting API (sandbox or production).
nodes.detail: Scope com.intuit.quickbooks.accounting. Env: QBO_CLIENT_ID, QBO_CLIENT_SECRET, QBO_ENV, QBO_REDIRECT_URI.

nodes.label: Google Places
nodes.summary: Primary address autocomplete and place details (US + CA), used because it catches new construction and new roads.
nodes.detail: Behind GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY. On REQUEST_DENIED or quota errors the proxy silently falls through to Photon.

nodes.label: Photon (OpenStreetMap)
nodes.summary: Free autocomplete fallback when no Google key is configured or Google errors.

nodes.label: Nominatim
nodes.summary: Geocodes a job address to lat/lng the first time a worker punches in; the result is cached back onto the project row.

nodes.label: Open-Meteo
nodes.summary: Current conditions for daily logs. WMO codes are mapped to sunny/cloudy/rainy/snowy, with wind >= 20 mph overriding to windy.

nodes.label: Vercel platform
nodes.summary: Hosts the SSR app and serverless route handlers, and fires the single declared cron.

flows.name: Sign in and session routing
flows.summary: How a request becomes a session, and where each role lands.

steps.title: Request arrives
steps.detail: Any non-asset path matches the middleware matcher.

steps.title: Resolve the session
steps.detail: createServerClient reads the request cookies, calls auth.getUser(), and mirrors any refreshed cookies onto the response.

steps.title: No user on a protected route
steps.detail: /dashboard, /projects, /directory, /approvals and /settings redirect to /login. A logged-out visitor on / goes to /homepage instead.

steps.title: Sign in
steps.detail: The login page calls signInWithPassword on the browser client.

steps.title: Session established
steps.detail: Supabase sets the cookie session; the access token becomes the bearer token every subsequent fetch attaches.

steps.title: Land in the office app
steps.detail: Middleware sends an authenticated visitor on /, /login or /signup to /dashboard.

steps.title: Unless they are field crew
steps.detail: The dashboard layout reads profiles.role and redirects FIELD_ROLES ('worker', 'member') to /field.

flows.name: Permission resolution
flows.summary: Role defaults, company overrides and per-user overrides collapse into one effective grid.

steps.title: Client asks for its grid
steps.detail: usePermissions fetches /api/me/permissions with the bearer token, appending as_user or as when an admin is previewing.

steps.title: Load the profile
steps.detail: Reads role, permission_overrides and company_id, degrading to role-only if the overrides column is missing.

steps.title: Layer the company's roles
steps.detail: company_roles rows for this company override the hardcoded defaults and define custom classes.

steps.title: Compute the effective map
steps.detail: resolveRoleBase picks the base map, then getEffectivePermissions applies per-user overrides resource by resource.

steps.title: UI hides what you cannot do
steps.detail: can(resource, action) gates sidebar entries, project tabs and buttons. ASSIGNED_ONLY_ROLES additionally see only projects they are on.

steps.title: Server re-check
steps.detail: getActor/actorCan mirror the same resolution so the API refuses what the UI hid. Wired into app/api/projects/route.ts and the settings permission endpoints; other handlers authenticate and scope by company rather than consulting the grid.

flows.name: AI quote scan builds the job
flows.summary: A photo or PDF of a contractor's estimate becomes budget lines and a payment schedule.

steps.title: Upload the quote
steps.detail: The Quote tab accepts a PDF or a phone photo of the estimate.

steps.title: Store and read the file
steps.detail: The file lands in Storage; the handler fetches it back as a buffer and picks a PDF document block or an image block by content type.

steps.title: Extract structure
steps.detail: claude-opus-4-8 returns JSON: total_amount, payment_terms, ordered payment_stages, and line_items with section, quantity, unit_price and amount. Code fences are stripped and the JSON is sliced between the outer braces; any failure returns null rather than throwing.

steps.title: Backfill older quotes
steps.detail: parseTerms() splits a free-text payment-terms paragraph into stages, so quotes scanned before structured stages existed still render as a schedule.

steps.title: User reviews the draft
steps.detail: Nothing is saved until the numbers are checked and edited on screen.

steps.title: Write the budget
steps.detail: Accepted lines become budget_line_items with sort_order; stages become the project's payment_stages.

flows.name: Request quotes from subs
flows.summary: Build a bid package, invite subs from the Directory, track who looked.

steps.title: Create the package
steps.detail: Scope, trade, description, due date and attachments.

steps.title: Persist it
steps.detail: bid_requests plus bid_request_attachments (or the older bid_packages set).

steps.title: Invite subs
steps.detail: One bid_invites row per invited company, each carrying an unguessable token.

steps.title: Sub opens the link
steps.detail: /bid/[token] needs no account.

steps.title: Mark viewed
steps.detail: First open flips the invite from 'invited' to 'viewed' and stamps viewed_at, which is what the GC's tracker shows.

steps.title: Nudge and revise
steps.detail: Remind and revision-request actions re-notify the sub without recreating the package.

flows.name: Sub submits a bid without an account
flows.summary: The public token page is a full quote builder.

steps.title: Open the token link
steps.detail: Middleware lets it through; no protected prefix matches.

steps.title: Load the request
steps.detail: GET /api/bid/[token] returns the package, project name and address, attachments, and any previous submission by this invite.

steps.title: Submit
steps.detail: Line items with quantities, unit prices, sections and payment terms are written as a bid_submissions row.

steps.title: Tell the GC
steps.detail: The submission is logged to project_activity and surfaces on the Bids tab.

steps.title: Registered subs get more
steps.detail: A sub with an account sees the same invite in My Bids, across every GC they work with.

flows.name: Award a bid (the cascade)
flows.summary: One click writes the subcontract, the payment schedule, the schedule bar, the notification and the activity entry.

steps.title: Award the winner
steps.detail: POST /api/projects/[id]/bids/[packageId]/award with the winning bid_id.

steps.title: Settle the package
steps.detail: Winner to 'awarded', every other bid on the package to 'rejected', package to 'awarded' - all three in one Promise.all.

steps.title: Create the subcontract
steps.detail: A subcontracts row inherits scope, trade and contract_amount from the bid.

steps.title: Stage the payments
steps.detail: The bid's payment_terms text is split line by line; a percent match becomes a percent stage with its dollar amount, anything else becomes a milestone, ordered by order_index.

steps.title: Put it on the schedule
steps.detail: If the bid carried duration_days and earliest_start_date, a schedule_items row is created for the date range.

steps.title: Tell the sub
steps.detail: A bid_awarded notification lands for the sub company's profile.

steps.title: Record it
steps.detail: project_activity gets 'Awarded "scope" to Company for $amount' with bid, package, company and amount in metadata.

flows.name: Vendor invoice to budget actuals
flows.summary: Approving (not paying) is what moves the money.

steps.title: Create the invoice
steps.detail: Against a subcontract, even when the sub has no account, or generated from line-item progress.

steps.title: Status flow
steps.detail: draft to approved to sent to paid, with client-paid vs escrow-paid split per invoice.

steps.title: Approval stamps the record
steps.detail: approved_at and approved_by_name are written, and the linked budget line's Actual accrues.

steps.title: Notify the sub
steps.detail: An invoice_approved notification tells them the amount cleared review.

steps.title: Log it
steps.detail: 'Invoice N approved - $amount' on the project activity feed.

steps.title: Print or attach
steps.detail: A printable invoice view, plus lien waiver attachments stored alongside.

flows.name: AIA pay application (G702/G703)
flows.summary: Monthly draws against the schedule of values, with retainage carried correctly.

steps.title: Start a draw
steps.detail: Only on projects whose billing_mode is progress billing; the Simple mode shows Invoices + Payments instead.

steps.title: Seed the lines
steps.detail: Every budget line becomes a pay_application_lines row with its scheduled_value.

steps.title: Carry previous work forward
steps.detail: Prior applications are summed per budget_line_item_id into previous_completed, so this period only asks for new work and stored materials.

steps.title: Compute G702
steps.detail: completed_to_date = previous + this period + stored; retainage = completed x retainage_pct; current_due = completed less retainage. retainage_pct defaults from projects.default_retainage_pct, then the company default, then 10%.

steps.title: Issue it
steps.detail: Draft to Submitted to Certified to Funded, with a printable G702 + G703 for the architect or bank. Works GC-to-owner and sub-to-GC.

flows.name: Client payment and escrow
flows.summary: Money in, fee out, and what is safe to release to vendors.

steps.title: Record the payment
steps.detail: Date, amount, method, memo, retainer flag and a QuickBooks-entered flag.

steps.title: Store it
steps.detail: client_payments, scoped to the project.

steps.title: Run the math
steps.detail: Received, contractor fee %, fee earned, available after fee, vendor billed and paid, escrow balance, outstanding to vendors, and projected cost vs invoiced.

steps.title: Answer the real question
steps.detail: The summary states what is safe to release to vendors right now given escrow and outstanding balances.

steps.title: Roll it up
steps.detail: Master Money aggregates cash in vs out, escrow and outstanding across every job.

flows.name: Clock in with selfie and geofence
flows.summary: A two-tap punch that is verifiable without being punitive.

steps.title: Tap clock in
steps.detail: The clock card captures a selfie and requests GPS, then posts multipart form data to /api/projects/[id]/time/punch. A punch without a selfie is rejected outright.

steps.title: Locate the job site
steps.detail: Uses projects.latitude/longitude if set; otherwise geocodes the address through Nominatim once and caches the result back onto the project row.

steps.title: Measure the distance
steps.detail: Haversine against a 250 m radius. Beyond it, or with no GPS at all, the punch is flagged for review - never rejected.

steps.title: Store the selfie
steps.detail: Uploaded to the daily-log-photos bucket under <projectId>/time/, then handed back as a long-lived signed URL.

steps.title: Write the entry
steps.detail: time_entries records coordinates, distance, the flag and the selfie URL. A second clock-in while one is open returns 409.

steps.title: Show the office
steps.detail: A time_clock_in activity entry appears immediately, marked (flagged) when relevant. Weekly totals feed timesheet approval and the payroll export.

flows.name: Daily log with photos and PDF
flows.summary: The day's record, filed from a phone in under a minute.

steps.title: Prefill the weather
steps.detail: /api/weather resolves lat/lon or geocodes the address, then maps Open-Meteo WMO codes to sunny/cloudy/rainy/snowy, with wind at or above 20 mph overriding to windy.

steps.title: File the log
steps.detail: Crew count, work performed, delays, visitors, and a signature.

steps.title: Attach photos
steps.detail: Photos go to the daily-log-photos bucket with a category, and render as thumbnails that open in a lightbox.

steps.title: Record the author
steps.detail: daily_logs stores who filed it; migration 060 backfilled authors on existing rows.

steps.title: Follow-ups and export
steps.detail: daily_log_updates adds later comments; the PDF route renders the whole log with pdf-lib for sending on.

flows.name: Pin a task on the drawing
flows.summary: Click the exact spot on the plan; the task and the notification follow.

steps.title: Drop the pin
steps.detail: Click the spot in the plan viewer, describe the work, assign a teammate, set a due date.

steps.title: Create the task first
steps.detail: A project_tasks row is inserted, then the plan_pins row is created pointing at it - so removing the pin leaves the task intact.

steps.title: Anchor it
steps.detail: Pins store normalised coordinates so they stay put while zooming, and are colour-coded per assignee.

steps.title: Tell the assignee
steps.detail: A task_assigned notification: 'You have been assigned a task from the plan'.

steps.title: It shows up in the field
steps.detail: The task appears in Field Mode's task list and on the project schedule; the pin list jumps the viewer back to the spot.

flows.name: RFI to answer link to change order
flows.summary: A field question routed to whoever can actually answer it.

steps.title: Raise the RFI
steps.detail: Numbered, with description and photo or file attachments. Subs can raise one through the portal without an account.

steps.title: Mint an answer link
steps.detail: rfis.answer_token backs a one-time public URL for the architect or designer.

steps.title: They answer
steps.detail: GET /api/rfi/[token] shows the question and attachments; the response and responder name are posted back. No account, no login.

steps.title: Close the loop
steps.detail: The RFI flips to answered and the project activity feed records it.

steps.title: Route the cost
steps.detail: An RFI carrying a change-order proposal (description, items, amount) lands in the Approvals inbox alongside invoices and other pending decisions.

flows.name: Request a COI by email
flows.summary: Ask once, the sub uploads through a link, the AI fills in the details.

steps.title: Request the document
steps.detail: Pick the sub and the document type: COI, licence, W-9, workers' comp or other.

steps.title: Mint the upload link
steps.detail: A compliance_requests row with a secret token; the sub gets the URL.

steps.title: Sub opens it
steps.detail: First open flips the request from 'pending' to 'viewed'. Partial uploads are allowed - they can come back for the rest.

steps.title: Scan the upload
steps.detail: The document is sent to Claude and lib/compliance-extract.ts normalises carrier, policy number, coverage and expiry into typed fields plus a human summary.

steps.title: File it
steps.detail: compliance_documents stores status (active / expiring_soon / expired) and expiry_date, per sub per project or company-wide.

flows.name: Nightly compliance expiry sweep
flows.summary: The only scheduled job in the system.

steps.title: Fire at 08:07 UTC
steps.detail: Declared in vercel.json. Authenticated by the x-vercel-cron header, or CRON_SECRET when called by hand.

steps.title: Find what is expiring
steps.detail: compliance_documents with an expiry_date inside the next 30 days and reminder_sent_at still null.

steps.title: Notify the owning company
steps.detail: Every profile at that company gets a compliance_expiring notification naming the document, the company and the days remaining.

steps.title: Stamp it once
steps.detail: reminder_sent_at is set and status becomes expiring_soon, so a document fires exactly once per expiry cycle.

flows.name: Snap a receipt into the budget
flows.summary: Photo to structured purchase to budget line, in one pass.

steps.title: Photograph the receipt
steps.detail: From the Materials page or a phone.

steps.title: Read it
steps.detail: Claude returns store, date, amounts, tax, category and line items from the image or PDF.

steps.title: Assign it
steps.detail: Pick the job, then link an existing budget line or create a new one on the spot - the same interaction as awarding a quote.

steps.title: Save the purchase
steps.detail: material_purchases stores the receipt image, the line items and a client_paid flag.

steps.title: Split the totals
steps.detail: 'Customer already paid' divides amounts into customer-paid vs owed-by-customer on Materials, Financials and Budget. Stores can be saved to the Directory as suppliers.

flows.name: Share the client portal
flows.summary: A read-only window on the job for the person paying for it.

steps.title: Generate the link
steps.detail: POST /api/projects/[id]/portal-token.

steps.title: Mint the token
steps.detail: 32 random bytes from crypto.getRandomValues, hex-encoded, written to projects.client_portal_token. Regenerating replaces the old link.

steps.title: Client opens it
steps.detail: /portal/[token] renders outside every authenticated layout.

steps.title: They see progress and payments
steps.detail: Job progress and payment stages, with no account and no access to anything else.

flows.name: Subscribe to the calendar feed
flows.summary: SyteNav dates inside Google, Apple or Outlook.

steps.title: Connect calendar
steps.detail: Settings mints profiles.calendar_token and shows the subscription URL.

steps.title: Calendar app polls
steps.detail: Calendar clients cannot send auth headers, so the secret token in the URL is the only credential. The feed is read-only by design.

steps.title: Build the iCal
steps.detail: Resolves the profile by calendar_token, collects the company's project dates, and emits VEVENTs with values escaped per RFC 5545.

flows.name: Connect QuickBooks
flows.summary: OAuth2 to Intuit, then a one-way push of accounting data.

steps.title: Click connect
steps.detail: The card only offers this when qboConfigured() sees both client id and secret.

steps.title: Redirect to Intuit
steps.detail: authorizeUrl() with scope com.intuit.quickbooks.accounting and a state row in quickbooks_oauth_states.

steps.title: Exchange the code
steps.detail: The callback swaps the code for access and refresh tokens over HTTP Basic, and stores them in quickbooks_connections.

steps.title: Sync
steps.detail: Phase 1 pushes from SyteNav to QBO against API minor version 73, sandbox or production by QBO_ENV, writing quickbooks_sync_log.

flows.name: Global search
flows.summary: One box across projects, customers, companies and files.

steps.title: Type a query
steps.detail: The global search component fires at two characters or more.

steps.title: Escape and fan out
steps.detail: Reserved PostgREST or() characters are stripped so a query containing a comma or percent sign cannot break the filter string.

steps.title: Return grouped hits
steps.detail: Each hit carries a title, subtitle and href, grouped by entity type for the dropdown.

flows.name: Super-admin impersonation
flows.summary: Real log-in-as for customer support, gated twice and logged.

steps.title: Open /admin
steps.detail: The email must be in SUPER_ADMIN_EMAILS.

steps.title: Pass the PIN gate
steps.detail: ADMIN_PIN is verified server-side, then an HMAC of the user id (keyed by the service-role secret) is set as a cookie and compared with timingSafeEqual - so the gate cannot be forged or replayed by another account.

steps.title: Pick the target
steps.detail: POST /api/admin/impersonate re-checks isSuperAdmin on every call.

steps.title: Mint a real session
steps.detail: auth.admin.generateLink produces a one-time magic-link token_hash the browser verifies, giving a genuine session as the target user rather than a simulated view.

steps.title: Log and banner it
steps.detail: impersonation_log records the event and a persistent banner shows who is being impersonated. Distinct from View As, which only previews another role's permissions.

flows.name: Invite a teammate
flows.summary: Email invite to accepted member with a role and a permission grid.

steps.title: Send the invite
steps.detail: Email plus a role, including any custom class the company has defined.

steps.title: Store it
steps.detail: company_invites holds the pending invite.

steps.title: They accept
steps.detail: /api/invite/accept and /api/complete-signup create the auth user and the profile, stamped with company_id and role.

steps.title: Grid applies immediately
steps.detail: Their first /api/me/permissions call resolves the role's defaults, any company override, and per-user overrides.

steps.title: Assigned-only roles need a project
steps.detail: Field supervisors, workers and read-only users see nothing until they are added on a project's Team tab.

flows.name: Ready for inspection to result
flows.summary: The sub raises a hand, the GC books it, the result gates the next stage.

steps.title: Sub marks work ready
steps.detail: From My Jobs, on their own scope.

steps.title: Notify the GC
steps.detail: An in-app notification asks them to book the inspector. Email and SMS for this are on the backlog.

steps.title: Schedule it
steps.detail: The inspection is requested and scheduled; it shows on the Master Calendar.

steps.title: Record the result
steps.detail: Pass or fail, with an AI-read inspection card where a document is supplied.

steps.title: Gate the money
steps.detail: A pass can release the next payment stage on the sub's schedule.

flows.name: Field Mode routing
flows.summary: Why a worker never sees the office app.

steps.title: Worker signs in
steps.detail: Same login as everyone else.

steps.title: Bounced out of the office app
steps.detail: The dashboard layout reads profiles.role and redirects FIELD_ROLES to /field before rendering any chrome.

steps.title: Field shell takes over
steps.detail: No sidebar, no project tabs, no company money. Bottom nav, idle logout, and a preview banner when an admin is looking.

steps.title: Four screens
steps.detail: Today, Tasks, Log, Me. Office roles that navigate to /field are sent back to /dashboard, except admins and managers previewing it.

flows.name: Activity and notification fan-out
flows.summary: The two write paths every feature shares.

steps.title: Any handler with a side effect
steps.detail: Roughly 40 route handlers call logActivity after they mutate something.

steps.title: One writer
steps.detail: project_activity rows carry project_id, actor name and id, type, message and a metadata jsonb.

steps.title: Read back two ways
steps.detail: The dashboard Recent Activity feed and the per-project activity drawer. Non-admins see their own actions; admins see everything.

steps.title: Notifications are separate
steps.detail: createNotification writes a per-user row that drives the bell: task_assigned, bid_awarded, invoice_approved, compliance_expiring and more.
